clauses.text: brainbase web:serve binds only to 127.0.0.1 (default port 31080), review:serve opens the same host, and the navigation lists only the screens that exist: today and objectives.

Every request whose Host is not a loopback name for the listening port is refused before any page, UI file or API is served; every non-GET request requires the launch token and the same origin; the shell carries a strict CSP and only allowlisted UI files are served. The value-proof review host behaves as before.

Objective reads and writes use the Foundation routes with the Graph owner id (or self) as principal, never a browser value; ACL, scope, storage, provenance and authorized uses are set by the host and rejected when sent; a stale update returns the current revision without saving; a save is verified by reading the new revision back.
Constraint references of an objective revision are shown read-only from applies_to relations to that exact revision; the Web never replaces them and hides the Story tab.

The World Model is read-only and shows variables and models with epistemic state and revision apart from observations with subject, value, occurrence, period, recording time, source and correction relation; without an approval reader only the adoptions section is reported as unverifiable.

Each screen shows the data directory, the Graph format and that no organization Graph is read; a Graph v1 data directory shows the migration commands instead of objectives or the world model, and the host never migrates or creates the data directory.

An empty list is shown only when absence is confirmed; failed, unconfirmed or partially unreadable collections are never shown as zero items, and unreadable records are counted with their reasons beside the readable ones.
The new UI parts and the shell take colors, fonts, radii and spacing only from the shared --bb-* tokens in ui/brainbase-tokens.css.

The objective editor's visible copy uses the information-architecture display words (目的, 評価基準, 変数, 制約, 版, 保存先, ストーリー) and never shows internal type, store, or API names such as Objective, Variable, Constraint, readiness, readback, FoundationRevisionStore, port, or COMPANY OS.
